- When sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 5–7 days show strong upward trend, reduce forecast slope after day 7 to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from neutral to positive, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.  
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model tends to hold high; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day starting day 5.
